test_prompts.title: No Drums
test_prompts.concept: 드럼 없는 곡 — Suno가 'no drums' 지시를 실제로 따르는가? 가장 기본적인 부재 테스트
test_prompts.sp: Pop rock song with absolutely no drums or percussion of any kind. The song must have no kick drum, no snare, no hi-hat, no cymbals, no tambourine, no shaker, no claps, no percussion loops — nothing that marks rhythm through hitting. The groove comes entirely from the bass guitar's rhythmic pattern and the guitar's strumming. The absence of drums should feel intentional and dramatic, like a room with one wall missing. Electric guitar strumming eighth notes for rhythm. Bass guitar playing a rhythmic walking line that implies the beat. Piano adding harmonic support. Vocals carry the melody. Absolutely no drums, no percussion, no rhythmic hits of any kind. 110 BPM implied by the bass line. Key of A major. 4/4 time.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Verse 1 — no drums]
(singing over drumless groove)
There is a space where the beat should be
A hollow where the rhythm used to live
Listen to the silence where the kick drum was
Listen to the nothing the snare forgave

[Chorus — still no drums]
(full vocals, guitar strumming, but NO drums)
We dance without a heartbeat
We move without a pulse
The music lives in the spaces
Where the drums should be

[Verse 2 — no drums]
(the absence is the feature)
The bass walks alone without a partner
The guitar strums against the air
Every note falls into the gap
Where percussion used to fill

[Chorus — no drums]
We dance without a heartbeat
We move without a pulse

[Bridge — no drums, stripped further]
(piano and voice only, no guitar even)
Just a voice
Just a chord
Nothing keeping time

[Final Chorus — no drums to the end]
(absolutely no percussion, ever)
We dance without a heartbeat

test_prompts.title: Gradual Exit
test_prompts.concept: 점진적 악기 퇴장 — 풀 밴드에서 시작해 하나씩 빠져나가 마지막에 1개만 남음
test_prompts.corpus_reference: fade(22회), stripping(0회), one by one(0회), exit(0회)
test_prompts.sp: Rock band piece that starts with all instruments and removes them one by one until only a single voice remains. The opening has full band at maximum: two electric guitars, bass, drums with double kick, keyboards, backing vocals, and lead vocals. Every sixteen bars, one instrument stops playing and does not return. First the keyboards drop out. Then the second guitar. Then the backing vocals. Then the drums simplify to just hi-hat. Then the bass stops. Then the hi-hat stops. Then the first guitar stops. The final section is completely solo voice with no accompaniment for thirty-two bars. Each exit should be noticeable — the listener should feel each absence. 95 BPM in F-sharp minor. 4/4 time.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Full Band — everything playing]
(all instruments, maximum)
We started with everything
Every voice every string every drum
The room was full of sound

[Keyboards exit]
(the pads disappear)
One color fades from the painting
Did you notice it go?

[Second guitar exits]
(the rhythm guitar stops)
The harmony thins
Two guitars become one

[Backing vocals exit]
(the choir vanishes)
The voices behind me are gone
I am singing alone now

[Drums simplify — only hi-hat remains]
(kick and snare disappear)
The heartbeat simplified
To a single ticking

[Bass exits]
(the low end vanishes)
The ground falls away
I am floating

[Hi-hat exits]
(the last rhythm stops)
No pulse now
No time

[Guitar exits]
(the last instrument stops)
Nothing but breath

[Solo Voice — 32 bars, no accompaniment]
(completely alone)
This is what remains
When everything is taken
Just a voice in an empty room
Singing to the walls
Singing to the absence
Singing to the space
Where the music was

test_prompts.title: Grand Pause
test_prompts.concept: 그랜드 포즈(GP) — 모든 악기가 동시에 멈추는 완전 무음 구간. Suno가 의도적 침묵을 생성하는가?
test_prompts.sp: Orchestral piece with three dramatic grand pauses where every instrument stops simultaneously and complete silence fills the space for four full beats. The music builds to a massive fortissimo climax, then every instrument cuts off at exactly the same moment. Four beats of absolute silence. Nothing. Not even room tone or reverb tail. Then the music resumes as if nothing happened. The second grand pause occurs during a quiet passage — the music simply stops mid-phrase for four beats of silence, then continues from where it stopped. The third grand pause is the longest — eight full beats of silence in the middle of the loudest passage. The silence should be jarring and physical, like the air being sucked out of the room. Full orchestra. 88 BPM in E-flat major. 4/4 time. Concert hall.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Build to Climax]
[full orchestra, fortissimo]
[brass, strings, percussion, woodwinds]
[building, building, building—]

[GRAND PAUSE 1 — four beats of absolute silence]
[NOTHING]
[every instrument stopped]
[four beats]
(the shock of sudden nothing)

[Music Resumes — forte]
[orchestra continues as if nothing happened]
(life returns)

[Quiet Passage]
[strings alone, piano dynamic]
[gentle melody flowing—]

[GRAND PAUSE 2 — four beats mid-phrase]
[SILENCE]
[the phrase interrupted]
(a door slammed in a whisper)

[Phrase Continues]
[strings pick up exactly where they stopped]
(the sentence finished after the pause)

[Massive Climax]
[FULL ORCHESTRA FORTISSISSIMO]
[THE LOUDEST POSSIBLE MOMENT—]

[GRAND PAUSE 3 — eight beats of silence]
[NOTHING]
[NOTHING]
[eight full beats]
(the longest silence, the deepest void)

[Final Phrase]
[orchestra, pianissimo]
[after the silence, everything is changed]
(sound means more after it was taken away)

test_prompts.title: Negative Space
test_prompts.concept: 네거티브 스페이스 — 음 사이의 여백이 음 자체만큼 중요한 곡. 미니멀리즘적 접근
test_prompts.sp: Jazz trumpet piece where the rests between notes are as important as the notes themselves. The trumpet plays short phrases of two to three notes separated by long silences of four to eight beats. Miles Davis late-period style — what is not played defines the music as much as what is played. The piano plays a single chord every eight bars, then silence. The bass plays one note every four bars, then silence. The drums play nothing except an occasional single cymbal touch every sixteen bars. The piece is ninety percent silence and ten percent sound. Every note exists in a vast empty space. The listener should be aware of the silence as a musical element, not as an absence of music. Trumpet, piano, bass, drums. 60 BPM implied. Key of D minor. Free time. Studio recording, very dry, no reverb.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Trumpet — three notes]
[then silence... four beats]
(the notes float in emptiness)

[Silence — eight beats]
(the silence is the music)

[Piano — single chord]
[then silence... eight beats]
(one color, then nothing)

[Trumpet — two notes]
[then silence... six beats]
(less is everything)

[Bass — one note]
[silence... four beats]
(the lowest voice, barely speaking)

[Long Silence — twelve beats]
(listening to the room)

[Cymbal — single touch]
[silence... sixteen beats]
(a whisper of metal, then gone)

[Trumpet — one note, sustained]
[fading into silence]
(a single thread dissolving)

[Silence — the longest gap]
(is the piece still playing?)

[Piano — final chord]
[held, fading]
(the last sound before nothing)

[Silence]
(the piece ends, but when did it end?)

test_prompts.title: A Cappella Pure
test_prompts.concept: 아카펠라 — 악기 완전 부재, 인간 목소리만으로 전체 곡 구성. Suno가 악기를 진정으로 '안 쓸' 수 있는가?
test_prompts.corpus_reference: a cappella(14회), acapella(3회), vocals only(2회), no instruments(0회)
test_prompts.sp: A cappella choral piece for mixed voices with absolutely no instruments. Four-part harmony: soprano, alto, tenor, bass. The soprano carries the melody. The alto provides harmonic support a third below. The tenor adds a countermelody. The bass sings the root notes and provides harmonic foundation. No piano, no guitar, no drums, no synthesizer, no beatboxing, no vocal percussion — only pure singing voices creating harmony. The blend should be warm and seamless, like a church choir. The piece moves through four-part chorale style in the verses and opens to six-part harmony in the chorus with divided sopranos and divided basses. Mixed choir of sixteen voices. No instruments of any kind. 76 BPM. Key of G major. 4/4 time. Cathedral acoustic with natural reverb.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Verse 1 — four-part harmony, no instruments]
(soprano melody, alto harmony, tenor countermelody, bass foundation)
When voices are the only sound
The air itself becomes the ground
No string no drum no key no reed
Just breath and tone are all we need

[Verse 2 — four-part harmony]
(same voicing, new words)
The human voice was first to sing
Before the hand could pluck a string
Before the stick could strike the skin
The song was always there within

[Chorus — six-part harmony, no instruments]
(divided sopranos, divided basses, fuller sound)
We are the instrument
We are the song
Every voice a string
Every breath a drum
We are all we need

[Verse 3 — four-part harmony]
(soprano solo then choir joins)
One voice begins alone
Then two then four then all
The harmony is not the notes
The harmony is that we sing at all

[Final Chorus — six-part, fortissimo then diminishing]
We are the instrument
We are the song
(voices fading one by one)
(until one voice remains)
(then silence)

test_prompts.title: Subtractive Arrangement
test_prompts.concept: 감산적 편곡 — 보통 편곡은 쌓아가지만, 이 곡은 빼면서 구축. 각 섹션이 전 섹션보다 더 적은 요소
test_prompts.corpus_reference: stripped(6회), stripped-back(3회), bare(8회), less is more(0회)
test_prompts.sp: Pop song with subtractive arrangement where each section has fewer elements than the one before. The intro has the maximum instrumentation: full band with strings, brass, backing choir, two guitars, bass, drums, keyboards, and lead vocal. Verse one removes the strings and brass. The pre-chorus removes the choir and second guitar. The chorus removes the keyboards. Verse two removes the drums. The bridge has only acoustic guitar and voice. The final chorus has only voice. The song gets quieter, simpler, and more naked as it progresses, the opposite of a normal pop arrangement that builds. The emotional impact increases as the production decreases. Starting with everything and arriving at nothing. 100 BPM in C major. 4/4 time.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Intro — MAXIMUM: strings, brass, choir, 2 guitars, bass, drums, keys, vocal]
(everything, overwhelming, lush)
This is the sound of everything at once

[Verse 1 — strings and brass removed]
(still full, but the orchestral shimmer is gone)
Already something missing
Can you hear the space where the violins were?

[Pre-Chorus — choir and second guitar removed]
(thinner, the support vanishing)
The voices behind me have left
The harmony is mine alone to hold

[Chorus — keyboards removed]
(guitar bass drums and voice only)
Stripped down to the bone
Every loss reveals what matters

[Verse 2 — drums removed]
(no pulse, floating)
The heartbeat stopped
But the song keeps going
Rhythm lives in the words now

[Bridge — acoustic guitar and voice only]
(almost naked)
Just six strings and one voice
This is all that's left
And it is enough

[Final Chorus — voice only, no instruments]
(completely bare)
Stripped down to the bone
Every loss reveals what matters
This voice
Alone
Is everything

test_prompts.title: Selective Exclusion
test_prompts.concept: 특정 악기만 선택적으로 제외 — 'no bass' / 'no guitar' 같은 네거티브 지시를 Suno가 정밀하게 따르는가?
test_prompts.sp: Three versions of the same rock song, each missing one critical instrument to test selective exclusion. Version A plays the full song without any bass guitar — drums, two guitars, and vocals only. The low end is completely empty, the music feels thin and top-heavy. Version B plays the same song without any guitar — bass, drums, keyboards replacing guitar, and vocals. The midrange loses its edge. Version C plays the same song without any vocals — full instrumental with guitar, bass, and drums. For this recording, play all three versions back to back as one continuous track with a two-beat silence between each version. Same melody, same arrangement, minus one different element each time. 120 BPM in E minor. 4/4 time. Rock production.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Version A — NO BASS GUITAR]
[drums, two guitars, vocals]
[the low end is gone, thin and top-heavy]
(singing)
Something is missing from below
The foundation crumbled and nobody knows
We play without the bottom
We play without the ground

[Two beats of silence]

[Version B — NO GUITAR]
[bass, drums, keyboards, vocals]
[the midrange edge is gone, smooth but toothless]
(singing)
Something is missing from the middle
The teeth are gone the bite is gentle
We play without the edge
We play without the fire

[Two beats of silence]

[Version C — NO VOCALS]
[guitar, bass, drums — full instrumental]
[the human element is absent]
[the melody exists only in instruments]
(no singing, the voice-shaped hole)

[Guitar plays the vocal melody]
[the absence of the voice is deafening]
(three versions, three absences, three different kinds of empty)

test_prompts.title: Fade to Nothing
test_prompts.concept: 페이드 투 낫씽 — 곡 전체가 사라지는 과정 자체가 곡의 내용. S010 시리즈 종합 테스트
test_prompts.sp: Ambient electronic piece that is entirely about disappearing. The track opens at full volume with a rich, layered soundscape: pad synthesizers, arpeggiated sequences, deep bass drones, shimmering high-frequency textures, field recordings of rain and wind, vocal samples. Over the course of five minutes, every element gradually fades to nothing. But this is not a simple volume fade — each layer thins independently. The arpeggio loses notes one by one. The pad narrows its frequency range. The bass drone drops in octaves until it is below hearing. The rain recording becomes more distant. The vocal sample becomes more and more reverb until it is just an echo of an echo. By the final minute, only a single sine wave remains, barely audible, then even that dissolves. The piece ends in absolute digital silence — not even room noise. Synthesizers, field recordings, vocal samples. No BPM — ambient, free tempo. No key — atonal drones.
test_prompts.lyrics:
[Full Soundscape]
[pads, arpeggios, bass drone, high textures, rain, wind, vocals]
(everything present, the maximum)

[Arpeggio Thinning]
[the arpeggio loses one note]
[then another]
[from eight notes to six to four to two]
(the pattern dissolving)

[Bass Descending]
[the drone drops an octave]
[then another octave]
[approaching the edge of hearing]
(sinking below perception)

[Rain Distancing]
[the rain recording moves further away]
[as if the window is closing]
(the world outside receding)

[Vocal Echo]
[the vocal sample drowning in reverb]
[an echo of an echo of an echo]
(the human voice becoming atmosphere)

[Pad Narrowing]
[the pad loses frequencies]
[high end gone, then low end]
[just a narrow band in the middle]
(the color draining)

[Almost Nothing]
[a single sine wave, barely audible]
(one frequency remains)

[The Sine Wave Fades]
[softer... softer...]
(is it still there?)

[Digital Silence]
[absolute nothing — not even room tone]
(the piece has ceased to exist)
